![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14040842/assets/ea3bc202dd0a40cfe096fb4170331fed39de28870aa355c776fd82de3b5db26b.png)

The quarter-ellipse above is defined by the parametric equations 

$$
x=5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $\theta ?$
worked_solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, $a=5$ and $b=2.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the *full* ellipse are

$$
x=5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a quarter-ellipse, we associate the parameter $\theta $ with the central angle formed by a point $(x,y)$ on the elipse and the $x$-axis. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14040842/assets/74714486ad225aba7111329be0c3853b7b922a852df450b057632e73fce5be6d.png)

We can see that if we restrict $\theta $ to $[0,\frac{\pi }{2}]$, we get the quarter-ellipse.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the quarter-ellipse are 

$$
x=5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,\frac{\pi }{2}].
$$
